## Natural history notes

A small flower fly characterized by its slender body, large reddish eyes, and yellow-and-black patterned abdomen with fine dark markings typical of calligrapher flies. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, roadsides, forest edges, parks, wetlands, and other sunny habitats with abundant flowers and low vegetation. Adults visit flowers for nectar and pollen, while the larvae likely prey on aphids and other small soft-bodied insects, making this species part of the beneficial predator community in gardens and natural areas.
